dimensions.note: The secret is written only to the configured vault and registered with the redactor; no resource, log line or return value carries it (tested). AWS credentials come from the SDK default chain, not config. The six credentials-sensitive-field warnings were examined and are false positives: accessKeyId (an identifier AWS documents as non-secret), two 12-hex fingerprints, and two vault ADDRESSES (accessKeyIdKey/secretAccessKeyKey). Marking them sensitive would vault identifiers and break CEL lookups. ISSUE: delivery uses context.vaultService.put/get, which is on MethodContext but undocumented for extensions; a swamp release could drop it. create's preflight fails closed (refuses to mint) if it is absent, so the failure mode is loud, not a lost key. The @swamp/1password backend also passes the value to the op CLI as argv; documented in the README.

Every method logs entry and completion with structured placeholders. Rollback logs at warn; a failed rollback logs a ROLLBACK FAILED line naming the orphaned key id. No secret in any log line (tested).

All preflight (target set, vault registered, slot available) throws before any mutating AWS call. Delivery failure and read-back mismatch roll the new key back before rethrowing with vault, item and cause. Rollback's catch is narrowed to NoSuchEntityException; anything else is surfaced. deactivate and delete read state back and throw if AWS returned 200 without effect.

15 unit tests with an injected fake IAM client and fake vault, no network permission: preflight ordering (zero AWS calls when vault missing), slot cap, happy-path delivery and fingerprints, secret absent from resources and logs, rollback on failed put and on read-back mismatch, delete refusing an Active key, deactivate->delete, delete of an unknown key, record carry-forward, inventory refresh, and the valid-target check. The fake writeResource now enforces swamp's per-execution instance-name uniqueness.

create is inherently non-idempotent (each call mints a new secret); re-running is guarded by the one-key refusal unless allowSecond, and the AWS two-key cap is enforced before calling AWS. Interruption after mint and before delivery is handled by rollback; if rollback itself fails the orphaned id is logged. delete of an already-gone key is a no-op.

ListAccessKeys paginates on IsTruncated/Marker. CreateAccessKey response is checked for both halves before use. GetAccessKeyLastUsed's 'N/A' sentinel is normalised to null. SDK default retry handles throttling.
No file handles or temp files. Every created key is tracked by id in the key resource and the inventory; a key that cannot be delivered is deleted.
README and tests use fictional names (heron-state, example-state) and AWS's documented example key id/secret. No account ids, hostnames, IPs or real vault names.
All schemas are plain z.object without passthrough; ids and item names are regex-constrained.
key and inventory: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 30.
create, list (sync equivalent), deactivate (the only mutable attribute is status) and delete.
valid-target check (policy label): targetVault/targetItem travel together and the item is a plain name. create additionally preflights vault registration and slot count before minting.

2026.09.23.1 shipped a collision this dimension exists to catch: create wrote key/current AND inventory/current in one execution, which swamp rejects ('Duplicate data instance name'), failing the run AFTER the key was minted and delivered. The previous review marked this pass without enumerating instance names across specs. Fixed: inventory instance is now 'summary'. The test fake now enforces per-execution instance-name uniqueness; negative control with the old name fails 3 tests with the production error.
Prior state is read with context.readResource, not the data repository.
Upgrade entry for 2026.09.23.2 added; no globalArguments change, upgradeAttributes is identity.
